Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Retail.AI is excited to move the pilot into a scoped deployment. Before we lock a Dedicated capacity proposal we need a realistic GPU sizing estimate tied to expected traffic so procurement can budget.

High-level:
- 10k authenticated users (web + mobile)
- Peak traffic window: 11:00–14:00 PT
- Use-case: conversational search + short assistive responses (average prompt 120 tokens, average response 140 tokens)
- Latency target: p95 <= 450ms for interactive sessions

Can your team run a quick estimator or send the template you prefer we fill? I can attach a sample traffic export if that helps.

Thanks,

Ben / Marissa —

Thanks — I started a quick pass on the CSV. To produce a defensible Dedicated sizing I need a few more discrete numbers. If you can paste answers inline or update the attached template (redwood_capacity_template_v1.csv) that speeds things up:

1) Peak concurrent sessions (users actively in a session) — e.g., 1.5k, 3k, etc.
2) Average request rate per active session (requests/minute).
3) Fraction of requests that use tool-calls or retrievals (adds 50–150ms extra per request).
4) Expected prompt length distribution: short (<=64), medium (65–512), long (>512) as percentages.
5) SLA tolerance: p95 latency target (ms) and whether occasional p99 spikes are acceptable.
6) Desired availability and failover region requirements.

Our quick rules of thumb we typically apply: 1x A100-80GB per ~600 sustained interactive qps for short responses (low-context), quantized variants can increase pack factor. But I need your distributions to tune batching & KV cache sizing.

Attaching the template.

-Mateo
Mateo Alvarez

Great, this is exactly what we needed. Quick summary of next steps from Redwood:

1) Baseline sizing: Mateo will publish a detailed spreadsheet (sizing_estimate_RetailAI_v1.xlsx) by EOD Monday that shows two configs:
